chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a pregnant woman who is given a divorce of the type that does not become effective until she marries another husband. He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Did you not tell me that if he has intercourse with her, he is not permitted to divorce her?' He said, 'Indeed, divorce is not valid except in a state of purity from which the menses have ceased, or in pregnancy from which the birth has become evident; and in this case, her pregnancy has become evident.'
ai.seo_question: Can a husband divorce his pregnant wife if the divorce is conditional on her marrying another man?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) resolves the apparent contradiction between the general prohibition of divorcing a pregnant wife and the specific condition that she must marry another husband before the divorce becomes effective. He clarifies that the phrase 'evident pregnancy' (ḥamluhā qad banat) refers to the physical manifestation of pregnancy, thereby allowing the divorce to take effect immediately upon the husband's declaration, provided the condition of subsequent marriage is met. This ruling underscores the precision of Shia jurisprudence in distinguishing between the state of pregnancy and the timing of the divorce's legal efficacy.
